title: COMMANDS — project lifecycle decisions
summary: Drill-down of “Project creation and date sync”: when a project is created from an ERP delivery address, how its dates follow the address, and how backfill sweeps fan out. Conceptual responsibilities, decisions and data transformations only; not a call stack or observed runtime behaviour.

sources.note: Lines 142-168: CreateProjectsFromErpReferences/HandleCustomerAddressChanged via HandleWithRetry; CreateMissingProjects/SyncProjectDates via HandleOnce.
Lines 35-90: skip existing project; build project from stored address (name=Address2, dates=ValidFrom/ValidTo); missing address throws; publish CustomerProjectChanged + PopulateOrderReferences.
Lines 34-69: missing project -> warn+return; align dates to address; inactive->active sends PopulateOrderReferences; CustomerProjectChanged always sent.
Lines 38-60: addresses missing a project, batched 100 -> CreateProjectsFromErpReferences. Lines 42-45 log non-Optimera tenant as unsupported but do not return.
Lines 36-53: project ids whose dates differ from address -> one HandleCustomerAddressChanged each. Lines 40-43 log non-Optimera tenant but do not return.
Opened full markdown (2023 workshop): project framed around delivery address; intent, not proof of current behaviour.

uncertainties: Which address changes reach this layer is decided in DOMAIN (layer:customerproject.func-app.domain-update).
Confluence 22779513 v4 delivery-address-as-project framing is design intent; not reconciled with code.
New nested layer id: auto-layout on first open; no dsp-arch-pos carryover; existing parent ids/positions unchanged.

nodes.label: COMMANDS queue (lifecycle subjects)
nodes.responsibility: Boundary input: CreateProjectsFromErpReferences, HandleCustomerAddressChanged (retry-handled), CreateMissingProjects, SyncProjectDates (handled once).

sources.note: Lines 142-168: CreateProjectsFromErpReferences/HandleCustomerAddressChanged via HandleWithRetry; CreateMissingProjects/SyncProjectDates via HandleOnce.

nodes.label: Create project from ERP reference
nodes.responsibility: Decision: project already exists for the reference -> skip (idempotent). Transform: stored CustomerAddress -> new CustomerProject (ProjectName = Address2, Start/End = address validity). No stored address -> failure that fails the whole batch message.

sources.note: Lines 35-90: skip existing project; build project from stored address (name=Address2, dates=ValidFrom/ValidTo); missing address throws; publish CustomerProjectChanged + PopulateOrderReferences.

uncertainties: Partial-batch behaviour on retry relies on the skip-existing check; retry/settlement internals are in Dahl.Core (not reviewed).

nodes.label: Align project with address change
nodes.responsibility: Decision: project dates differ from address validity -> overwrite project dates. Decision: project transitions inactive->active -> request order-reference population. Always republishes CustomerProjectChanged, even without date changes.

sources.note: Lines 34-69: missing project -> warn+return; align dates to address; inactive->active sends PopulateOrderReferences; CustomerProjectChanged always sent.

uncertainties: IsActive derivation lives on the model; not re-derived here.

nodes.label: Backfill sweeps
nodes.responsibility: Fan-out only: finds addresses without projects (batches of 100) and projects with drifting dates, and re-enqueues them as the two per-item commands above. Intended Optimera-only.

sources.note: Lines 38-60: addresses missing a project, batched 100 -> CreateProjectsFromErpReferences. Lines 42-45 log non-Optimera tenant as unsupported but do not return.
Lines 36-53: project ids whose dates differ from address -> one HandleCustomerAddressChanged each. Lines 40-43 log non-Optimera tenant but do not return.

uncertainties: Code logs non-Optimera tenants as unsupported but continues; whether that is intentional is unresolved (source-vs-intent conflict, not fixed here).
Trigger for sweeps (manual/timer) not evidenced in reviewed source; deferred.
